bib.venue: preprint (dated March 26, 1999); in Advances in Large Margin Classifiers, MIT Press, to appear

question: How can the uncalibrated output of an SVM be mapped to a calibrated posterior probability P(y=1|x) while keeping the SVM's sparseness?
hypothesis: A two-parameter sigmoid fitted discriminatively on SVM outputs matches the empirically observed posterior and gives probabilities comparable in quality to a kernel machine trained with a regularized likelihood.
contributions: A post-hoc sigmoid P(y=1|f)=1/(1+exp(Af+B)) fitted by maximum likelihood on unbiased SVM outputs
Bayes-motivated non-binary targets t+=(N+ +1)/(N+ +2), t-=1/(N- +2) as regularisation against overfitting
Comparison of SVM+sigmoid against raw SVM and a regularized-likelihood kernel machine on three tasks
Pseudo-code for a Levenberg-Marquardt style model-trust fit

method.summary: Train an SVM unchanged, obtain unbiased outputs f_i by 3-fold cross-validation (or a hold-out set), then fit A and B of a sigmoid by minimising cross-entropy against smoothed targets with a model-trust (Levenberg-Marquardt) optimiser. Compare error counts and negative log likelihood against a raw SVM and a kernel machine trained with regularized binomial likelihood.
method.task: binary classification probability calibration (post-hoc Platt scaling)

datasets.name: UCI Adult (income from census data)
datasets.size: Linear: 32562 train / 16282 test; Quadratic: 1605 train / 16282 test; 123 inputs
datasets.source: Merz and Murphy 1998 (UCI); inputs quantized as in Platt 1999 (SMO)

datasets.name: Web page category from key words
datasets.size: Linear: 49749 train / 21489 test; Quadratic: 2477 train / 21489 test; 300 inputs

models.name: SVM + sigmoid
models.architecture: SVM (linear; quadratic kernel) with 2-parameter sigmoid on output

other.C: Reuters Linear 0.08; Adult Linear 0.05; Adult Quadratic 0.3; Web Linear 1.0; Web Quadratic 10.0
other.kernels: linear; quadratic k=(xi.xj+1)^2/14 (Adult), /12 (Web); constants are average self dot product

models.name: Regularized likelihood kernel machine
models.architecture: kernel machine, logistic link, negative log multinomial likelihood + lambda ||h||^2 (Wahba)

training.objective: SVM: C*sum(1-y_i f_i)+ + 0.5||h||^2 (eq 3); sigmoid: min -sum t_i log p_i + (1-t_i) log(1-p_i), p_i=1/(1+exp(A f_i+B)) (eqs 11-12)
training.optimizer: model-trust / Levenberg-Marquardt (Gill, Murray, Wright 1981; Press et al. 1992), max 100 iterations
training.steps: up to 100 iterations; stop when |gradient|<1e-9 or objective change tiny for 3 iterations
training.regularisation: target smoothing t+=(N+ +1)/(N+ +2), t-=1/(N- +2); SVM C and regularisers set per algorithm on hold-out set
training.compute: 3-fold CV costs about 2.2x a single SVM on the full set; hold-out (30%) about 1.5x if SVM training scales quadratically

other.lambda_update: x0.1 on success, x10 on failure, give up at lambda>=1e6
other.sigmoid_training_set: 3-fold CV outputs f_i; training-set outputs are biased (margin examples forced to |f|=1) and for non-linear SVMs can be disastrously biased

metrics.name: Number of test errors
metrics.definition: misclassifications on test set; raw SVM at f=0, SVM+sigmoid at P=0.5

metrics.name: -log(p) score
metrics.definition: negative log likelihood of the test set (sum over test examples)

eval.protocol: McNemar's test for error differences, Wilcoxon signed rank test for log-likelihood differences, p=0.05; underlined entries in Table 2 are significantly better than non-underlined ones.

results.claim: Reuters Linear: raw SVM 1043 errors, SVM+sigmoid 963 (significantly better), regularized likelihood 1060; NLL 3249 for sigmoid vs 3301 for regularized likelihood (sigmoid significantly better).
Adult Linear: raw SVM 2441, SVM+sigmoid 2442, regularized likelihood 2434 errors; NLL 5323 sigmoid vs 5288 regularized likelihood (latter significantly better).
Adult Quadratic: raw SVM 2626, SVM+sigmoid 2554 (significantly better), regularized likelihood 2610 errors; NLL 5772 sigmoid (significantly better) vs 5827.
Web Linear: raw SVM 260, SVM+sigmoid 265, regularized likelihood 248 errors; NLL 1121 sigmoid vs 958 regularized likelihood (latter significantly better).

Web Quadratic: raw SVM 444, SVM+sigmoid 452, regularized likelihood 507 errors; NLL 1767 sigmoid vs 2163 regularized likelihood (sigmoid better on total log likelihood, but Wilcoxon prefers regularized likelihood).
results.note: Text says Wilcoxon rank test prefers regularized likelihood for Web Quadratic although sigmoid has better overall NLL; the table underlines 2163 for the regularized likelihood (read as image, 1767 vs 2163 as printed with underline on 2163).

results.claim: On Adult Quadratic the sigmoid threshold P=0.5 corresponds to f=-0.1722, a better threshold than f=0; zero is not necessarily Bayes optimal for a raw SVM, mostly when the class prior ratio is far from one (Reuters Linear and Adult Quadratic).

Qualitative: a sigmoid fits the non-parametric posterior estimate (Bayes rule on 0.1-wide histogram bins) extremely well even beyond the margins for a linear SVM on Adult; class-conditional densities are not Gaussian and show discontinuities at f=+1 and f=-1.
results.setup: Linear SVM on UCI Adult, 3-fold CV, bins 0.1 wide

results.claim: Neither SVM+sigmoid nor regularized likelihood dominates: sigmoid makes fewer errors on 3 of 5 tasks; regularized likelihood gives significantly better probabilities on 3 of 5.

limits: Only binary SVMs; five task configurations from three datasets, no calibration metric such as reliability diagram or ECE, only error count and test NLL.
Smoothing targets and sigmoid form justified empirically (Figs 1-2) and by MAP argument; no theory for the shape of class-conditional densities ('currently under development').
Fitting on the SVM's own training outputs is biased, especially for non-linear SVMs; needs hold-out set or CV (extra cost 1.5x to 2.2x).
The sigmoid cannot model dependence of P(y=1|f) on other feature-space directions u; it averages over u.
Paper is dated 1999; modern neural nets and LLMs are not covered. Any mapping to LLM P(True) or temperature scaling is the reader's, not the paper's.

terms.definition: P(y=1|f)=1/(1+exp(Af+B)): output of SVM assumed proportional to the log odds of a positive example, with A and B trained discriminatively

figures.caption: The histograms for p(f|y=+-1) for a linear SVM trained on the Adult data set. The solid line is p(f|y=-1), while the dashed line is p(f|y=1). Notice that these histograms are not Gaussian.
figures.why: Shows why not Gaussian and motivates the sigmoid

figures.caption: The fit of the sigmoid to the data for a linear SVM on the Adult data set (as in Figure 1). Each plus mark is the posterior probability computed for all examples falling into a bin of width 0.1. The solid line is the best-fit sigmoid to the posterior, using the algorithm described in this chapter.
figures.why: Best single picture of a sigmoid calibration map against empirical posterior bins

figures.why: Errors and NLL for raw SVM, SVM+sigmoid, regularized likelihood
